content:
{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Primary endpoint analysis method not specified",
      "quote": "The primary endpoint in the study is the percent change in EASI score from baseline to week 16.",
      "page": 27,
      "section": "4.2.1",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The statistical section does not describe the specific analysis method (e.g., mixed model, ANCOVA) for the primary endpoint, nor the estimand attributes (population, variable, intercurrent events, summary measure) beyond the variable and summary measure.",
      "fix": "Add a detailed primary analysis section in the SAP or protocol specifying the statistical model, covariates, and handling of intercurrent events (e.g., rescue medication, discontinuation)."
    },
    {
      "title": "Secondary efficacy endpoints lack analysis methods",
      "quote": "Proportion of patients achieving EASI-50, EASI-75, and EASI-90 (≥50%, ≥75%, and ≥90% improvement from baseline) at week 16",
      "page": 27,
      "section": "4.2.2",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The statistical section does not specify analysis methods for the secondary efficacy endpoints (e.g., logistic regression, time-to-event analysis for pruritus onset). Only the primary endpoint and selected secondary endpoints are mentioned in the hierarchy.",
      "fix": "Provide analysis methods for each secondary efficacy endpoint in the SAP, including model details and handling of missing data."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing estimand attributes for primary endpoint",
      "quote": "The primary endpoint in the study is the percent change in EASI score from baseline to week 16.",
      "page": 27,
      "section": "4.2.1",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The estimand for the primary endpoint is incomplete: population (FAS is defined later), variable (percent change in EASI), intercurrent events (not specified), summary measure (difference in means) are not all stated together.",
      "fix": "Define the estimand explicitly, including how intercurrent events like rescue medication use or early discontinuation are handled."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing handling of missing data",
      "quote": "For continuous variables, descriptive statistics will include the following information: the number of patients reflected in the calculation (n), mean, SD, median, first quartile (Q1), third quartile (Q3), minimum, and maximum.",
      "page": 66,
      "section": "10.4",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The statistical section does not describe how missing data will be handled for the primary or secondary efficacy analyses (e.g., multiple imputation, mixed models with missing-at-random assumptions).",
      "fix": "Add a section on missing data handling, specifying methods for primary and secondary endpoints."
    },
    {
      "title": "Multiplicity control incomplete",
      "quote": "To control the overall family-wise type I error rate of 5%, a hierarchical procedure from high to low dose will be performed for the primary endpoint and selected secondary efficacy endpoints (eg, EASI-75, IGA score of 0 or 1 and a reduction from baseline of ≥2 points responder at week 16) across the REGN3500 dose regimens vs placebo.",
      "page": 65,
      "section": "10.1",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The hierarchy is not fully specified; it only mentions 'selected secondary efficacy endpoints' and defers to the SAP. This leaves ambiguity about which endpoints are included and the order of testing.",
      "fix": "Specify the full hierarchy in the protocol or state that it will be finalized before database lock, but provide a complete list of endpoints in the hierarchy."
    },
    {
      "title": "Sample size does not account for dropout",
      "quote": "the enrollment of 60 patients per treatment group will provide 96% power to detect a 35% difference between the most efficacious REGN3500 SC dose and the placebo group with respect to percent change in EASI score from baseline to week 16, assuming the common standard deviation (SD) is 50%, with a 2-sided test at the 0.05 significance level.",
      "page": 66,
      "section": "10.2",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The sample size justification does not mention any inflation for dropout or missing data, which could reduce power if patients discontinue before week 16.",
      "fix": "State whether the sample size accounts for expected dropout and provide the assumed dropout rate if applicable."
    },
    {
      "title": "Exploratory endpoints not analyzed",
      "quote": "Any exploratory endpoints will be described in the statistical analysis plan (SAP).",
      "page": 27,
      "section": "4.2.2",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The exploratory objectives (e.g., biomarkers, QOL) are listed but no analysis methods are provided in the protocol; they are deferred to the SAP, which may be acceptable but leaves a gap in the protocol.",
      "fix": "Consider adding a brief description of exploratory analyses in the protocol or ensure the SAP is referenced clearly."
    },
    {
      "title": "Primary analysis timing may affect final analysis",
      "quote": "A primary analysis of the study may be performed when the last patient completes 16 weeks of treatment duration, in order to expedite the potential interactions with regulatory agencies to design future phase 3 studies.",
      "page": 68,
      "section": "10.4.3.1",
      "category": "advisory",
      "severity": "advisory",
      "explanation": "The interim primary analysis is stated to be final for primary and secondary endpoints, but the protocol does not specify how this affects the analysis of week 36 safety endpoints or whether the unblinding could bias later assessments.",
      "fix": "Clarify that the primary analysis will not affect the conduct of the study and that week 36 safety analyses will be performed after final database lock, as implied but not fully detailed."
    }
  ]
}
